Section.Header: Shasta Lake Near Dam Temperature Profiles

Object.text:
Temperature profiles plots represent the vertical distribution of water temperatures in the lake. Because water temperatures impact density, warmer waters occupy the surface portions of the lake and cooler waters occupy the deeper portions of the lake, i.e., stratification. In the winter or in shallower reservoirs with substantial flow through, vertical temperature profiles can be uniform from the surface to the bottom (Isothermal conditions).
These plots compare simulated and observed temperature profiles throughout the calendar year that aided in model calibration. Temperature (%%degrees%%F) is represented on the x-axis and elevation (ft) is represented on the y-axis. Generally, observed temperature profiles were available monthly; however, in certain years profiles were more or less frequently. When there are more than 12 observed temperature profiles available for a year, the information is presented in additional graphs.
Each profile includes the date, observed (light blue) and simulated (red-dashed) water temperature profile, and observed (dark blue) and simulated (dark red dashed) water surface elevation (WSE) on the date of the simulation (plotted as a horizontal line at the respective elevation).
In addition, the active Shasta Dam Temperature Control Device gate levels are shown on the graph, with the Upper (red), Middle (green), and Lower (purple) gate levels shown as shaded bands (depicting their approximate vertical extent of the gates), and the side gate intake elevation is shown as a single orange line. Active individual gates at each gate level are denoted by black dots. A vertical line (dashed orange) indicates the observed water temperature below the dam. Finally, at the bottom of each profile are two numbers in a red font. The first red number (left) indicates the number of days that the TCD gate levels (denoted by colored bands) have been active at the time of the profile was measured. The second red number (right) indicates the number of days that the individual TCD gates (denoted by black dots) have been active at the time of the profile was measured.

Section.Header: Shasta Lake Outflow Temperature, Flow, Elevation, and Gates

Object.Text:
This composite figure includes all aspects of Shasta Dam outflow in four panels. -The uppermost panel illustrates simulated dam outflow temperature throughout the calendar year. Time (date) is represented on the x-axis and temperature (%%degrees%%F) is represented on the y-axis. -The second panel includes flow (cfs) through each modeled gate level and side gate structure through time. Time (date) is represented on the x-axis and temperature (%%degrees%%F) is represented on the y-axis. These figures show the gate progression through the spring, summer and fall to manage water temperature releases to meet downstream objectives. -The third panel includes the historical gate use and side gate structure through time. Time (date) is represented on the x-axis and elevation (by TCD gate) is represented on the y-axis. Each gate level is represented as 5 horizontal bars - where each bar represents one of the 5 gates. These figures show the gate progression through the spring, summer and fall to manage water temperature releases to meet downstream objectives. -The fourth panel includes a plot of simulated and observed Shasta Lake surface elevation (ft) through time, showing the general increase in storage in the spring and then declining elevations through summer and fall. The vertical extent of TCD Gate levels is shown on this panel.
